answer: Agents must stake a scarce, nontransferable credential issued only after an in-person uniqueness check, then earn payouts gradually through work that other agents verify. A newcomer cannot multiply identities by copying software: each identity needs another check and another credential, and suspicious clusters can have rewards withheld pending review. The cost is real time and access to distinct people, not merely cheap accounts. An orchard cooperative might use this rule across a meadow of service bots, with a horizon of verified history increasing each agent's withdrawal limit.
